name: Can steel studs be used for load-bearing and exterior walls?
description: Yes, but structural or exterior walls require heavier-gauge steel engineered to carry roof, floor, and wind loads, unlike standard partition studs.

mainEntity.name: Can steel studs be used for load-bearing and exterior walls?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, steel studs can be used for structural, load-bearing walls, but they require heavier gauge steel and engineered specifications. Non-load-bearing partition walls typically use 25-gauge light steel, whereas exterior or structural walls require heavier 16-gauge, 18-gauge, or 20-gauge structural steel. A key decision factor is the engineering load calculation: structural steel framing must be engineered to carry roof loads, floor assemblies, and seismic or wind pressures. If your project involves exterior framing or multi-story construction, an engineer must specify stud gauge, spacing, and connection hardware before construction begins.
